newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK BONDS RALLY ON RATE CUTS,ECU/DRS BREACHES 311.
newsitem.headline: GREEK BONDS RALLY ON RATE CUTS,ECU/DRS BREACHES 311.

text.p: Greek bonds were surging in early dealings sparked by the finance ministry's move to cut T-bill rates by 60 basis points, ecu/drachma breached 311, depos dipped and forex forwards were trading lower, traders said.

"Bonds are red hot after the finance ministry slashed rates on T-bills by 60 basis points," a senior bond dealer at a private bank said. "This goes for all types of debt paper and especially fixed coupon bonds."
The finance ministry announced it will cut three-, six- and 12-month T-bill rates by 60 basis points to 8.6 percent, 8.9 and 9.7 percent respectively effective today.
"Depos are down 10 to 20 basis points from two-week to 12-month tenors and implied drachma rates from forex forwards are lower 20 to 25 basis points," said a trader at a private bank.
Bank of Greece offered to drain up to 200 billion drachmas of 14-day funds at 11.90 percent in today's depo auction.
Fixed-coupon bonds and FRNs were on a bull run with prices surging 50 to 60 basis points, bond dealers said.
Ecu/drachma opened firmer breaking out of the 311 level on some ecu buying from abroad dealers said.

"Ecu opened up and is currently trading around 311 on ecu buying from abroad," said a forex dealer at a foreign bank. "The market is awaiting to see what the central bank will do later on at the fixing."
The dealer said the strength of the ecu against the drachma could relate to three foreign currency-linked government loans that expire in the next few days.
The mark was quoted at 159.58/63 from Tuesday's 159.595 fix, the dollar at 272.06/16 drachmas from 270.980 and the ecu at 311.01/11 from 310.520 drachmas.
